# Desensitized session history fixtures

These files feed the read-only session parsers of the Records page. They contain no real credentials, user paths or private conversation content: titles and message text are replaced with neutral placeholders while structural fields, event shapes and token counts keep the observed wire form. Fixtures for the legacy CLIs document Codex (`codex-0.158.jsonl`, `codex-last-usage.jsonl`), Claude Code (`claude-2.1.jsonl`), Grok (`grok-1.0/`), Pi (`pi-0.87-v3.jsonl`) and OpenCode sessions.

The 2026-10 default-off additions contribute:

- `zcode-3.14.4-model-io.jsonl` — the bundled agent's model-io rollout log (session messages with per-turn token counts), desensitized from the real 3.14.4 install; `zcode-3.14.4-task.json` is the matching legacy task snapshot shape.
- `kimi-code-0.31.1-wire.jsonl` — one `agents/main/wire.jsonl` stream: `context.append_message` user prompts, `content.part` assistant segments (same `turnId` joins into one message) and `usage.record` per-call token totals with `inputOther`/`output`/`inputCacheRead`/`inputCacheCreation` split buckets. Subagent streams contribute additional usage events with wire-scoped ids (regression: multi-agent streams must not overwrite each other in `history_usage`).
- `dsh-0.2.1-v3.frames` / `dsh-0.2.1-v4.frames` — checksum-chained zstd session frames. The byte layout is a constructed contract: the official documentation describes the frame chaining without a byte-level specification, so these fixtures are generated by the in-test encoder and asserted byte-identical. The first real `.frames` sample from a machine install must confirm the layout.
- `codebuddy-2.161.1-session.jsonl` — a `projects/*.jsonl` session transcript sanitized from real local data; usage totals come from assistant `providerData.usage` only (turn-metrics `tokenDelta` is not a billing figure).

Session parsing is read-only: the adapters never rewrite native history. Parsing fixtures do not establish live session acceptance for any CLI version.
